fact: ITWeb reports that the Information Regulator was established on 1 December 2016 to monitor and enforce compliance with POPIA and PAIA, and that its chairperson Pansy Tlakula and executives were speaking for it in September 2026.
The Information Regulator imposed its first fine, R5 million, on the Department of Justice and Constitutional Development for breaching POPIA, according to ITWeb quoting the Regulator.

The Regulator also fined the Department of Basic Education R5 million, and the Electoral Commission and Lancet Laboratories R100,000 each, both paid; the document gives no dates for these (published 2026-09-02).

The Regulator issued the South African Bureau of Standards an enforcement notice the week before 31 August 2026 over its 2024 ransomware attack, finding POPIA conditions for lawful processing violated and giving it 90 days to revise policies, run impact assessments and implement security measures.

After a November 2023 POPIA assessment the Information Regulator issued the basic education department a notice not to publish the 2024 matric results in newspapers; the department kept publishing exam numbers.
The Regulator lost three bids in the Pretoria high court to stop newspaper publication of matric results and has taken the case to the Supreme Court of Appeal (reported 17 August 2026).

The Information Regulator published on 20 May 2026 an enforcement notice against Central Johannesburg TVET College, finding breaches of POPIA conditions for lawful processing and of the section 22 duty to notify security compromises, and ordering registration of information officers, notification of data subjects, an apology, a compliance framework and training within set periods.
The Information Regulator, through its Enforcement Committee, issued the POPIA enforcement notice of 20 May 2026 and runs an eServices Portal on which information officers are registered.
The regulations were made and signed on 27 February 2026 by Adv Pansy Tlakula as Chairperson of the Information Regulator.

The Information Regulator is stated to have announced on 7 April 2025 a requirement that breaches be reported through its eServices Portal, and receives breach notifications under POPIA, so it is an existing body acting.

The Information Regulator, on the Enforcement Committee's report, found FT Rams Consulting in breach of POPIA sections 12, 18 and 69 over unsolicited direct-marketing emails, and ordered it to stop and to file an undertaking, privacy policy, impact assessment and compliance framework within 90 days.
